submission.natural_language_explanation: L1/H2 is a broad, dense previous-token pass-through head: its attention at each position is split between the immediately preceding token (mean weight ~0.35 over prose, but 0.80-1.00 at the positions that peak), the position itself (~0.29) and the text's first token (~0.14), and what it writes is W_O applied to the value of whichever token it lands on, so its strength above the 0.883 floor is |W_O(v_attended - mean write)| - how unusual the attended (almost always preceding) token is, not what the current token means (the current token only sets the query, hence how sharply attention lands). It therefore peaks at 0.25-0.7 x max when the preceding token is substantive or unusual - existential 'there' before is/'s/were (0.6-0.7 x max), the first piece of a word the tokenizer splits (p|ang, Ch|ag, br|im, Sch|re, S|atur, 0.3-0.7), 'all'/'last'/'third' before a noun (0.3-0.55), a verb before its pronoun or particle (told him, handed him, sat down, came back), over/on/across/behind before 'the' (0.25-0.35), comma-separated digit lists (0.35-0.6) - and sits at 0-0.05 x max whenever the preceding token is 'the'/'The'/'a', a period or comma, or 'in'/'to'/'of'/'at'; so ordinary prose of 12+ tokens is where this head is broad and straddles the line (measured peaks 0.15-0.5 x max, 33 of 50 sentences above the line), while only texts of 2-7 tokens built from the commonest words ('The N.', 'The N is ADJ.', 'The N V the N.', 'The N is on the N.', one single-token word + '.') are reliably inactive (0 of 61 measured).

rival_explanations: The head fires on the token it lands on, not on the one before it: its real triggers are rare or technical current tokens (digit runs, proper-name pieces, LaTeX, non-Latin script fragments), which is the reading the scan's 63% token-identity confound suggests, and it predicts that swapping the preceding token leaves the peak unchanged while swapping the current token kills it.

It is a lexical collocation detector that fires on tight, frequent word pairs ('there is', 'on the', 'all afternoon', 'told him') because of their specific identity, so a rare or ungrammatical predecessor before the same following word ('zorble the') should stay below the line even though the predecessor is unusual.

It is a word-boundary head that only fires where the tokenizer splits a word or emits whitespace runs (the 14 top examples that peak on a fragment), and the single-token pairs 'there is', 'on the' and 'told him' are tokenizer side effects, so single-token collocations with no fragment in them should be quiet.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The men arrived in the hall. The band began to play. The crowd stood still.
